rely

rih-LYE · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To rely is to depend on someone or something for support.

Remote villages rely on the weekly supply plane for medicine and mail.

Example

Since losing his sight, Mr. Okafor has relied on his guide dog to get through the busy market safely.

He depends on the dog's help and trusts it to keep him safe -- that dependence and trust is what it means to rely on someone or something.

How rely sits among its neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

depend

depend: to need someone or something's support

trust

trust: to believe someone will come through for you

Antonyms

doubt

doubt: to feel unsure that someone will really help you

disregard

disregard: to pay no attention to; to ignore

How Strong Is It? — expect → rely → depend

expect vs. rely

expect vs. rely: To expect help is just to think it will come -- to rely on it means you've built your plans around it.

depend vs. rely

depend vs. rely: Depend is rely's closest partner, and often even stronger -- if you depend on something, you may not manage at all without it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back; again (Latin)

Root — ly

Root — ly: to bind, to tie (from Latin ligare, 'to bind,' worn down to -ly through French lier)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- ('back') + ly ('to bind,' from Latin ligare, worn down through French lier): to rely originally meant to bind yourself back to something — you tie your plans to what you trust will hold.

Use the root in a new word: ligament

Use the root in a new word: ligament: The skater strengthened the ligaments in her ankle before returning to the ice.

Root Check

Word Choice

Rely is always about dependence and trust, and it takes 'on' or 'upon': you rely on a friend, a bus schedule, a backup plan. It never describes physically leaning against something -- a hiker leans on a walking stick, but relies on a map.
